newsitem.title: UK: ISDA voices concern over U.S. derivatives plans.
newsitem.headline: ISDA voices concern over U.S. derivatives plans.

text.p: A leading derivatives industry group said on Tuesday it was "concerned" by proposals made by the U.S. Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) for the disclosure of derivatives on balance sheets.

The proposals, set out by FASB in June, may lead to increased financial risk, discourage risk management and cloud financial statements, the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) said at a media briefing in London.
FASB's proposals would require all derivatives to be carried on the balance sheet as assets ot liabilities at fair, or market value.

"Although we are sympathetic to the FASB's desire to clarify certain anomalies that currently exist in the accounting framework, the ... proposed approach will not reflect the economics of a company's current or future risk management activities," ISDA chairman Gay Evans said.

Evans said a second set of proposals, set out by Britain's Accounting Standards Board (ASB) and covering all financial instruments, would give a better picture of a firm's economic and risk management position.

ASB's approach would encourage firms to provide some quantification of the market risk of the financial instruments and the presentation of a "big picture" of their objectives in using derivatives and other financial instrumnets, Evans said.
But she said FASB's proposals were both complex and limited.
"(This) might well discourage appropriate risk management activities, leading to increased financial risk while detracting from the clarity and usefulness of financial instruments," she said.
